reconciliation.method: exhaustive enumeration of aggregate_parent_phase over every (generationStatus x downloadStatus x validationStatus x finalApprovalStatus) tuple: 840 single-variant combinations plus 100 two-variant representative pairs, counting single-step transitions only

reservedPhases.DOWNLOADING: Design intent only. ParentTaskPhase.DOWNLOADING is referenced 0 times in backend/src and aggregate_parent_phase never returns it (proven by exhaustive enumeration). The key is kept because test_machine_contract_matches_enums requires one key per enum value.
reservedPhases.VALIDATING: Same as DOWNLOADING: referenced 0 times in backend/src and never produced by aggregate_parent_phase.

reconciliation.whyTheOldContractWasWrong: Version 4.3.2-phase1 declared 12 real edges illegal, including the two most common ones (GENERATING -> DELIVERABLE and GENERATING -> AWAITING_FINAL_APPROVAL). The aggregate returns only 5 phases and any of them can follow any other, so the old table described a DOWNLOADING -> VALIDATING -> AWAITING_FINAL_APPROVAL pipeline that the implementation never walks. This drift is why assert_transition was never wired into the write path.
reconciliation.safetyBoundary: For the 5 aggregate-reachable phases the transition table is deliberately a complete graph and therefore carries no ordering guarantee. What actually protects correctness is cas_task_phase: a conditional UPDATE on (id, phase, state_version) that raises VersionConflictError when rowcount != 1. Do not read this table as an authorization gate for those 5 phases.
reconciliation.overPermissive: This table is a canary, not a reachability model. Where an aggregate source can never co-occur with a given aggregate output (for example QUEUED -> DELIVERABLE) the edge is still listed so the write-path check never raises a false alarm. Tightening those pairs needs per-call-site evidence that does not exist yet.

parentTask.notes: restingStates are where the system rests once work concludes, but aggregate_parent_phase can still move a task out of them (for example when a variant is re-run or rejected after delivery), so they are not terminal. Only CANCELLED is terminal, and _aggregate_task guards it.
